mechanism_crosswalk.first_falsifiable_question: Under the same evaluator-call budget, does explicit novelty/semantic control increase unique untouched-OOS survivors rather than only reducing duplicates?
Does selective reuse reduce repeated invalid/duplicate trials and evaluator calls per OOS survivor without narrowing diversity?
Can an independent verifier detect seeded fabrication, leakage and artifact/result mismatches with useful precision/recall?
Does structured evolution beat fresh independent generation on OOS survivors per fixed evaluation budget?
Does adaptive allocation improve survivor yield after controlling for model, data, seed and total evaluator calls?
Does joint optimization beat a frozen-model factor-only search on untouched OOS after equalizing total research compute?

findings: No tracked alpha-discovery family currently has an investor2 matched head-to-head verdict; all remain BLOCKED for frontier purposes.

The landscape is not one algorithmic race: the families attack distinct bottlenecks including novelty control, memory reuse, executable reproducibility, evolution, adaptive allocation and factor-model coupling.
AgonAlpha is currently a registry gap relative to the Issue #194 canonical family registry and must not become the organizing authority merely because it was investigated most recently.
The first experiments should compare mechanism groups with low confounding and high information gain before attempting full-paper reproductions or combining many mechanisms.
